verdict.rationale: Zep ships a first-party Memory MCP Server that lets end users connect MCP clients such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor to their Zep memory, which allows natural-language operation of memory through those assistants. The Graphiti MCP server offers similar access but is labeled experimental. Zep itself has no native natural-language command interface: its primary surfaces are the SDK API and the zepctl CLI, and the language understanding comes from the external MCP client. Missing for 10: a native natural-language command interface, evidence of which operations (admin, deletion, graph management) can be done via natural language, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: The Memory MCP Server lets an end user connect an MCP client (Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others) to their own agent memory in Zep.
This enables AI assistants like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and VS Code with Copilot to interact with Graphiti's Context Graph capabilities, providing persistent context and contextual awareness.
The Graphiti MCP Server is an experimental implementation that exposes Graphiti's key functionality through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
